_meta.role: full configuration: Trace-as-State ordering + System-1 governance (selection via the association graph)
_meta.status: run set for the next round (C0, C1, C2)
_meta.note: The project's own configuration: TAS on, recall selection on, x first; `xFirst: true` and `deliver: true` come from `cellPolicy('C2')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) and are not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell. The arm it has to beat is C1, TAS alone: if the full configuration cannot beat the stabiliser without System-1, the System-1 half has not earned its place.
_meta.planGateRemoved: This file carried `planGate: { on: true, ... }` until 2026-10-02, and round `20261002-2037` is why it no longer does. That round - the one this cell was written for - contains **zero** `plan_gate` records: not in its control plane (6 546 records), not on its tape (2 003 lines), not in its session stream, across 277 steps and 289 tool calls. The gate can be reached in exactly two ways, a numbered or bulleted plan in an assistant message (`extractPlans`) or a `todo/write` session event (`extractTodoEvent`), and that run produced neither: the model wrote prose and reasoning, and the event stream carries no `todo/write` at all. So the arm advertised an ordering step it never ran, in the one cell whose whole purpose is to be the full configuration. The knob is removed rather than given a new path, because adding one would change what C2 *is* mid-study - a new plan source means new System-1 calls, and the C1-vs-C2 comparison the file's own `note` rests on would no longer be between the two cells that were run. Nothing takes over the gate's role: the honest reading of round `20261002-2037` is that C2's ordering half was TAS alone, exactly as in C1, and the difference between the two arms was recall selection. `packages/core/src/types.ts` carries the full decision; the mechanism itself (`packages/core/src/plan-gate.ts`, `packages/dsh-plugin/src/plan-gate-runtime.ts`) is kept and still tested for whichever arm next has a plan source the model actually writes to.
_meta.retry: `s1.retryAttempts: 2` is set below per docs/CELLS-RUN.md's setup, and this cell needs it most: C2 makes an order of magnitude more System-1 calls than the other two arms, the shared Laya refuses rather than queues at its admission limit, and a measured round lost 732 of 2 016 calls to `503 server busy` - a refused call falls back to the local lexical scorer, so an unrecovered refusal turns an S1-governed cell into a partly lexical one. The retry waits the server's own `Retry-After` and is answered, and `attempts`/`waitedMs` on the `s1_call` record report how often it was needed; report `judgedPairs / scoredPairs` either way.
_meta.admissionLimit: `s1.admissionLimit: 8` is new, and it is the other half of the same problem `retryAttempts` addresses. A retry is the right answer to *one* refusal; it is the wrong answer to a backend refusing everything, because the retry is one more request inside the same admission window. Round `20261002-2037` measured what that costs: 5 992 `s1_call` records over a 2 219.7 s span - **2.70 requests/second** - of which **3 859 (64.4 %)** were refused with `503 {"detail":"server busy"}`, the refusal rate above a third in every thirty-second bucket of the run, 4 057 of them carrying `attempts: 2` and 4 057 000 ms of `waitedMs` between them, for a yield of `judgedPairs / scoredPairs = 4 152 / 860 672 = 0.48 %`. The local Laya admits 16 concurrent requests and refuses the rest; one cell saturated it by itself, because the upkeep queue drains several events per tick without awaiting its async handler, so several scoring loops were in flight at once. The plugin now caps what this cell may have in flight at this number and opens a circuit breaker after a run of refusals, probing once per cooldown until the backend answers again. A window the gate does not send is **deferred**, not scored lexically: the graph holds its cursor over it, the pair is not counted in `scoredPairs`, and it is counted in `deferredPairs` on the assembly record instead - so `judgedPairs / scoredPairs` stays the share of what was offered that the backend answered, and the omission is a number with a reason rather than a lower coverage nobody can see.
_meta.provider: `s1.provider` below names the lane this cell runs. It is `laya-serve`, the **local** backend at `http://127.0.0.1:8008`, and the live per-cell profile pins `s1.baseUrl` to that address (docs/CELLS-RUN.md's setup) - so the value here has to be the one the profile overrides it with, or the file describes a lane no cell uses. It previously read `jev`, the earlier **remote** System-1 service, which is not what any run has used and which would additionally have needed an API key it does not have: a reader who took that value seriously would look for a credential that nothing requires. What a cell actually ran is recorded, and can be re-read, from its own `kind:"wiring"` tape record - `verify-wiring.mjs` asserts it - so treat that record, not this file, as the authority.
